title: Bind rendered packet sections and framing with explicit integrity

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as the canonical manifest digest plus terminal byte-counted whole-envelope SHA-256 trailer.

provenance.review_target: Reported 396-file MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Bind the whole packet, not just the manifest. The individual file hashes bind exact source. The manifest hash likely binds the index. It is not obvious whether it also binds symbol outlines, omissions, edge declarations, ordering, and task text. I would publish section hashes and a final packet hash: index_sha256, symbols_sha256, content_merkle, packet_sha256.
feedback.normalized_claim: Make the integrity coverage of every semantic and rendered section explicit, and consider a final hash that binds the packet framing itself.

current_behavior: manifest_sha256 hashes the canonical compact JSON manifest.
The manifest includes ordered files, source hashes, projections, outlines and symbols, omissions, and edge declarations.
Exact file hashes transitively bind reconstructed source bodies, but the manifest does not bind textual framing, chunk boundaries, terminator choices, or the embedded guide.
The optional task is intentionally excluded from manifest and packet identity so reusable context identity remains task-independent.
evidence: src/context.test.ts: task independence and digest tamper tests
docs/context-format-v3.md: Canonical JSON manifest and optional task

proposal.summary: Evaluate explicit integrity domains for semantic manifest state, rendered sections, exact content, framing, and optional task without introducing self-referential hashing ambiguity.
candidate_changes: Document exactly which fields and order the existing manifest hash binds before adding more hashes.
Define canonical byte serializations for index, symbols, edges, omissions, and content-root calculation.
Add section hashes only when they enable partial retrieval or verification that the manifest hash cannot already provide.
Define a packet hash over a canonical packet with the packet-hash field omitted or stored in a final trailer.
Keep task identity separate or define an optional instruction hash without changing reusable context identity.
non_goals: Do not imply that the current manifest hash covers raw rendered packet bytes.
Do not add high-entropy hashes repeatedly without a concrete verification use.
Do not accidentally make reusable packet identity task-specific.

questions: Is semantic equivalence or byte-for-byte rendered packet identity the desired top-level guarantee?
Which sections need independent verification for partial retrieval?
Should chunking and terminators be integrity-bound even when reconstructed source already matches the file digest?
How should the final packet hash avoid self-reference?
risks: Section hashes may duplicate the canonical manifest and dilute model attention.
A raw packet hash makes harmless deterministic-renderer changes compatibility-sensitive.
Poorly specified canonicalization produces cross-implementation hash disagreements.
Binding task text to context identity harms cache and artifact reuse.
evidence_needed: A formal integrity-domain map for every current packet field and byte range.
Independent implementation tests for canonical section hashes and final packet hashing.
Partial-retrieval scenarios demonstrating which independent hashes are operationally useful.
Token-cost comparison for candidate integrity records.
